The Weserstadion (Weser Stadium) is a multi-purpose stadium in Bremen, Germany. Scenically situated on the north bank of the Weser River, it is surrounded by lush green parks (the name 'Werder' is a regional German word for “river peninsula”).

The city center is only about a kilometer away.

It is the home stadium of German Bundesliga club SV Werder Bremen since 4 February 1899, having a maximum capacity of 42,100.

Weserstadion is a football stadium in Bremen, Germany. The Weserstadion is scenically situated on the north bank of the Weser River and is surrounded by lush green parks (the name 'Werder' is a regional German word for "river peninsula"). It is the home stadium of German Bundesliga club Werder Bremen. Opened in 1924, this oldest stadium has a capacity of around 42,100-43,087 spectators, provides luxurious VIP rooms, and serves as a hub for sporting and music events. Long History: The stadium has been used by SV Werder Bremen since 1909, making it one of the oldest sporting venues in Germany. Nordderby Match Center: Home to the fierce rivalry between Werder Bremen and Hamburger SV. Museum & Tours: There is a club museum and stadium tours to learn about Werder Bremen's history. content: # Wohninvest Weserstadion. ## Wohninvest Weserstadion – stadium description. However it wasn’t until 1926 that the ground received its first grandstand. Then in 1930’s the name Weserstadion became common due to proximity of Weser river. Around the same time Werder Bremen and less known Bremer SV started using the venue, with first one becoming permanent tenants and the latter moving out in 1963. WWII period was unstable for both naming and use of the ground. In 1934 the Nazis renamed it to Bremer Kampfbahn and it became political rally spot. This time, however, it was used mostly for American sports and between 1945-1947 called IKE-Stadion. Then Weserstadion became prevalent once again and so it stayed. In 1992 it became Germany’s first ground to have skyboxes, receiving further commercial and office space in 1997’s redevelopment of the East stand. In the 2024/25 season, the German Bundesliga once again confirmed its status as one of the most spectacular and well-attended football leagues in Europe.
